informed.diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: The most frequent recoverable failure is off-by-one fingertip-pair selection during near-contact holds, undercounting the "6" hand as "7" (s000006, s000007, s000008, s000016), which drags down near:10x10, near:6x6, near:9x10 (all 0.0), near:8x7 (0.33), transition (0.207), and classes 6x7/
informed.patch_hypothesis: Measurement (not the diagnosis's pair-selection guess) showed the dominant recoverable failure is near_contact holds where the correct fingertip pair is found but its distance sits just under the 0.35 contact threshold, so `contact` flips true when the label expects false (near:10x10/6x6/9x10 all at 0.0, near_contact_accuracy 0.41 baseline).
informed.patch: Lowered CONTACT_THRESHOLD from 0.35 to 0.2975 (the best passing value from `--sweep-all`), no other logic changed.
informed.expected: near_contact classes (near:10x10, near:6x6, near:9x10, near:6x10, near:10x8) improve most since their pair selection was already right and only the boolean flag was wrong; near_contact_accuracy rises 0.41→0.73 and overall exact_match 0.458→0.487 with no class losing more than 5 points and false_unknown_rate unchanged at 0.036.
